# A component spliced with a literal prop has that prop folded into its body,
# and an assignment's index is part of the body: the optimizer folded the
# value written but never the target, so `names["b/{slug}"] = "B {slug}"`
# became `names["b/" + slug] = "B x"`, naming a parameter of a component that
# no longer existed. html raised "slug is not defined" as the page loaded --
# the Pokédex's test of a move's name, its lookup written with a literal slug.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var names map[string, string] = {}

component lookup(kind string, slug string) ui.node {
    if kind == "a" {
        effect(@mount { names["a/{slug}"] = "A {slug}" })
    } else {
        effect(@mount { names["b/{slug}"] = "B {slug}" })
    }
}

component holder ui.node {
    lookup(kind="b", slug="x")
}

func testTheWriteIsKeyedByTheArgument(t test.Test, c holder) {
    t.wait(func() => names.get("b/x", "") != "", 2000)
    t.assert(names.get("b/x", "") == "B x")
}

ui.window {
    holder
}
